utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We trust that in the intervening days counsel have been able to get on top of the matters that were creating difficulties and which led to us having the interruption. Your next witness, I see, is here, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The next Prosecution witness is Ms. Vilma Ruskovska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness please stand. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is on the card given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. I take it you're receiving a translation in a language that you're more familiar with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Mr. Saxon has some questions for you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is your name Vilma Ruskovska?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And have you lived your entire life in what is now Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is it your ethnic background Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you currently a deputy public prosecutor in the department for organised the crime in the republic prosecutor's office in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: In the public prosecutor general office in the Republic of Macedonia. All the rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. And in August of 2001, were you a deputy public prosecutor in the basic public prosecutor's office in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall providing a statement to members of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in December of 2005?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on this past Monday, the 4th of June, 2007, was that statement certified by a presiding officer from the registry of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, at that time, did you have an opportunity to review a copy of your statement in your native Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, at that time, this past Monday, did you make an addendum to your statement which corrected and clarified certain portions?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, when read together, are the contents of your certified statement and the addendum true and correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would tender the statement of Ms. Ruskovska that has been certified under Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm told that the interpreters did not hear what the court officer just said.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. Exhibit P235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, Witness Vilma Ruskovska is an ethnic Macedonian and a deputy public prosecutor in the general public prosecutor's office in Skopje. In August of 2001, the witness held a position of deputy public prosecutor in the basic public prosecutor's office in Skopje. This witness's evidence speaks to her professional activities in relation to the events arising out of the attack on the village of Ljuboten on 12th of August, 2001. The witness describes the work performed by her and other public prosecutors and investigative judges that led to the production of criminal indictments against a number of Ljuboten villagers for alleged participation in terrorist acts. The witness speaks of the inability of the investigating authorities, at that time, to conduct an on-site investigation in Ljuboten after the 12th of August, 2001. The witness also states that her office made no efforts to interview the police officers who were deployed in Ljuboten in August 2001, and she explains the reasons why no such efforts were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, I just have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I could ask that the addendum to Ms. Ruskovska's 92 bis statement be shown, if that would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, do you see a copy of that addendum in your language on the right side of the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I notice that one of the witness's microphones is not turned on. Perhaps if I could ask the usher to turn on the microphone on her right side, please. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to briefly ask you about what is listed in item 4 in this addendum. In that paragraph, in those additional sentences that were added to paragraph 13 of your statement, you say the following. There's a sentence, it's actually the second sentence of that of that paragraph, and it begins: "I also received a threat from the NLA. For example, either in late July 2001 or after the events in Ljuboten, I received a telephone call in my office. The caller was a man who threatened to come and kill me and rape me." I'd just like to explore this with you for a moment, please. Whoever was calling you, they knew where you worked?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: They knew your telephone number?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: They called the phone number of the public prosecutor's office, basic public prosecutor's office. It is listed in the phone book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you feel after you received that telephone call?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I was frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you continue to do your work?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You had received a threat, which made you frightened, yet you decided to continue with your professional responsibilities. Why?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. You, as a Prosecutor, you know that our profession is such. We do receive threats, but we need to continue working having this in mind. We either accept our job as it is, or we discontinue working at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At that time in 2001, did you carry a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I ask, approximately, how tall you are?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Before I begin my cross-examination of the witness, Ms. Vilma Ruskovska, I wish to inform Your Honours that only I will examine Ms. Ruskovska. The Counsel of Mr. Tarculovski will not make use of their time. Therefore, I ask Your Honours to allow me to put all my questions because, apart from the fact that the witness was performing a certain duty in 2001, she is, if I may so express myself, an expert witness of sorts who can explain to us the overall procedure. She is the only representative of the public prosecutor's office to be called here, so I ask that I be allowed to put all my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are grateful for Mr. Apostolski's cooperation. You certainly will be able to have a more expansive time than otherwise, but we ask you not to forget the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Ms. Ruskovska.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and I appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. We have come across each other before, have we not?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, you understand the language I'm speaking. I understand the language you are speaking. For this reason, your response my question might come very quickly. I ask you, however, to bear in mind that both my question and your response have to be interpreted, so that Their Honours and the other participants in these proceedings can understand what we are saying. That's why I ask you to wait a little until my question is interpreted, and only then to begin your answer. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When answering a question by my learned friend, you said that you are now working on organised crime and corruption in the public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have been working in the public prosecutor's office for nearly 17 years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, more than 17 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you have already told my learned friend, in 2001, you were deputy prosecutor in the public prosecutor's office in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, the lower public prosecutor's office in Skopje was carrying out its prosecutions before the lower court in Skopje; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, before the Basic Court Skopje I and Basic Court Skopje II.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your professional duties, which you're still carrying out today, you are certainly aware of the legal rights and responsibilities of the organs participating in criminal proceedings in the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you're aware of the rights and responsibilities of the organs conducting investigations and carrying out certain investigative activities in the investigative phase of the proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, is it correct that all the organs in the Republic of Macedonia participating in criminal proceedings are duty bound do comply with the law of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when conducting criminal proceedings a strict legal procedure has to be respected, and no organ can undertake to carry out the duties and responsibilities of another organ unless this is provided for by law. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that persons acting contrary to the law would be violating the criminal procedure; and under the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia, a violation of the criminal procedure can be a ground of appeal and the judgement can be rendered null and void for this reason. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I would just like to say that if they act in contravention to the law, if they act in breach of the criminal code, they will be held criminally responsible and criminally prosecuted. But if they act in breach to the law of criminal, then that procedure will not be valid before the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 2001, the Republic of Macedonia was facing terrorist attacks by terrorist Albanian groups from Macedonia and some groups from Kosovo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The whole country, the Republic of Macedonia, was not affected by the attacks, but the attacks affected the town of Tetovo, the area around Skopje, and the town of Kumanovo. So this would be the north and north-western parts of the country. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: It is correct. It is only that in the vicinity of Skopje towards Kumanovo it was taking place, while the other part towards Velic and the other areas were not affected. There was nothing there. So not the entire surrounds of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that at that time in the Republic of Macedonia no state of war had been declared?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: It was not declared.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because these were isolated terrorist attacks and because no state of war had been declared in the country, the criminal proceedings you participated in were carried out according to domestic law?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time you, as deputy prosecutor; your colleagues; and judges in the court, before which you were acting, were not even considering applying international humanitarian law to certain events. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have already said that the competences of various organs are prescribed by law. If I say that the public prosecutor's office is an independent organ carrying out its activities in compliance with the law, I would be correct, would I not?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The public prosecutor and his deputies acting in criminal proceedings are elected by the Macedonian parliament to which they are responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor and his deputies are authorised and have certain powers in criminal proceedings, and these are precisely regulated by the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Law on Criminal Procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work and the performance of your duties, you cooperate with other state organs, including certainly the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior does not have any kind of authority over the prosecutor's office or any powers over its work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Authorised officials of the Ministry of Interior also perform their duties in compliance with the Law on the Ministry of Interior and the Law on Criminal Procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have been active for many years, it is clear to you that most police work, especially detection, falls under the purview of authorised officials in the various sectors and departments of the Interior Affairs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to make things easier for the witness and to speed up my cross-examination, I have prepared a set of documents I wish to put to the witness. I have a binder for all the members of the Trial Chamber, one for the witness; and for the purposes of e-court and the transcript, I will give all the 65 ter numbers or exhibit numbers. But the documents are also separated by tabs which have numbers. So make it easier to find them, I will also give the tab number of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, would you please now take a look at 65 ter number 1D-180, Macedonian page 1D-1951, English 1D-1963. It is found under tab 1 of the binder which is before you. This is the Law on the Public Prosecutor's Office which was in force in 2001. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems it's not in e-court. This is exhibit 65 ter number 1D-180, Macedonian page 1D-1951, and the page in English 1D-1963.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Article 5 on this page, it says that at the proposal of the government, the Macedonian Parliament appoints the public prosecutor and his deputies, as you said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please turn the page and look at 1D -- Macedonian 1953 and English 1D-1964 -- no, 1963, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at Article 15 on the public prosecutor's office. Is it correct that this Article prescribes the rights, duties and, powers of the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. These rights and duties refer both to pre-trial proceedings and to the stage where the criminal proceedings are conducted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, the question may be superfluous; but to clarify criminal procedure in the Republic of Macedonia, I wish to ask you: Is it correct that in compliance with the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia, criminal proceedings begin when a decision on an investigation is carried out -- is issued against a certain person because there are grounds to suspect that that person has committed a crime. Is that when criminal proceedings begin?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The procedure that precedes the issuing of such a decision in compliance with the law is the basis for the pre-trial proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Pre-trial procedure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this period, also in the pre-trial proceedings, the public prosecutor has significant powers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has such powers in connection to detection and in guiding other organs in detecting the perpetrators of crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Well, essentially detection of crime is done by or organs. We can, for instance, ask. If we hear that a crime has been committed, we could then order that the competence institution, the institution competent for that, conducts the pre-trial procedure, so to detect whether somebody really perpetrated a crime, which crime et cetera, while the actual prosecutor's office is still not an operational body. To detect crime, we depend on other state organs, the police, customs administration and other ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Article 15, in fact, describes the duty of the prosecutor, and it says that the public prosecutor's office takes care of prompt and efficient revealing of criminal and other punishable acting and their perpetrators, and this is what you have just described. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, but in cooperation with other competent state organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Competency is carried out in compliance with Article 16, which states that the prosecutor carries out this duty in cooperation with other bodies for detecting crimes and other competent bodies and legal persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This same Article 15 also establishes the powers of the prosecutor's office in criminal proceedings. The public prosecutor submits or files a motion to initiate a criminal investigation. In compliance with the law, he takes measures and activities to ensure the proper conduct of the proceedings. He issues an indictment. He declares regular and irregular legal remedies and means and undertakes other activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I will just correct you with regards to the economic crime. We do not file indictments. It is the other competent bodies that do this. Only if a criminal report indicates that it is not a crime, criminal offence, rather, an economic crime, then we do it; then we file charges, but this is an exception. Otherwise, all the rest that you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please look at the document under tab 2 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is 65 ter 1D-181, Macedonian page 1D-1968, page in English 1D-1992. Your Honours, this document is also Exhibit P88, but this exhibit does not have a translation into English, which is why we have extracted the articles we intend to use with the witness and provided an official translation so that Your Honours can follow. This is the reason why we have presented it as a special Defence -- as a separate Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're grateful for that, Ms. Residovic. Thank you very much. Could I just mention that you will appreciate that we do not really need a basic course on criminal procedure. It would be useful to have the main provisions pointed out to us, but I don't think you need to spend a lot of time with the witness going over what the provisions mean. As long as they're identified in the evidence, they are pretty ease to follow, so I'm just letting you know that you can move along fairly quickly through this, if it will help you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I will dwell on only a few of the provisions, because our client is charged with failing to take measures so that some of the provisions in the Law on Criminal Procedure relate to issues of the competences of various organs in carrying out the procedure of detection, as well as the powers of the Ministry of Interior. So I will very briefly put my questions, by your leave. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you to look at this document. And in the law on page 1D-1968, Article 42, the version in English is on page 1D-1992. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The powers of the public prosecutor are again provided for, this time under the Code of Criminal Procedure for the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In point 1 of this Article, again, the responsibilities of the public prosecutors are mentioned in the pre-trial procedure, so it is obliged to take the necessary measures in the detection of the criminal acts and of the perpetrators and in order to direct the pre-trial procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the other points, the competences are made -- are delineated for the roles of the prosecutor in the criminal procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to see the provisions of Article 140. That is found in the Macedonian page 1D-1974; in the English version, page 1D-1996 -- 1997; Article 142, that is. It is -- it stipulate what the prosecutor needs to do if he receives a certain criminal report or when he realises that certain criminal act might be perpetrated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the -- this Article stipulates the competences of the Ministry of Interior, not of the prosecutor, in the detection of the criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. That Article regulates the duties of the Ministry of Interior. I apologise. Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that all state bodies and institutions have the duty to report crimes that are prosecuted ex officio?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This Article that we're looking at - and you warned me rightly, and the mistake was mine - speaks about the role in the detection of crime of the Ministry of Interior. In relation to this, I wish to ask you: Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that the Ministry of Interior could not interrogate citizens when they appear as witnesses?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. They can only take a statement from them if we want to voluntarily give the statement, and that statement is not valid before the court. But to interrogate them as witnesses, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have just stated that the statement would not be valid before the court. Actually, all the statements of suspects and other persons must be separated from the court file and the court's decision must not be based on them; is that correct? Is it only the court, the institution that could interview the person in the capacity of a witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: According to the Law on Criminal Procedure, that was valid until 2004. Only the court, that is, only the investigating judge or a presiding judge on the main trial, were able to take a statement. Whether from an accused or from a witness, that will be valid and would serve as evidence before the court. With the changes of the Criminal Code of December 2004, now the public prosecutor can also take statements, both from accused as well as from witnesses, of course, sticking to the procedure. If it is -- if that is an accused, his counsel should be present, and the statements given in the premises of the public prosecutors office and before the public prosecutor can also serve as evidence. But let me repeat, this is according to the Criminal Code that was adopted in December 2004 -- the Law on Criminal Procedure. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. Maybe I forgot to mention at the beginning. I will ask you to speak about the Law on Criminal Procedure and the competences of individual bodies in 2001 at the time when the events that are noted in the indictment took place. Is it also correct that the court is the only body that could issue a decision on detention of a person?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, upon a proposal of a public prosecutor. But only the public prosecutor is the one who gives the proposal and the decision. Whether a person will be detained or not is made by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The authorised officers of the Ministry of Interior could keep a person for up to 24 hours, and after that only if they had the approval of the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. They were able to hold the person for 24 hours, and after the 24 hours they should either file criminal charges or should set the person free. If they file charges against the person, so before the 24-hour deadline would expire, they were supposed to take the person before an investigating judge; first, to bring the charges before the public prosecutor, so that they could study it and assess whether there is a base or suspicion whether a criminal act has been perpetrated. And if they assess -- if the prosecutor assesses, then he files a request for initiation of an investigation with the measure of detention, and at that time the person is brought before the investigating judge, who, after the -- the interview, would decide whether the person would be put in detention or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the Article 144 that have you in front of you, which I read and quoted by mistake as a provision governing the situation covered in Article 142. Actually, this Article is found in the Macedonian page 1D-1975, and the English version is 1D-998. So, Ms. Ruskovska, I'm particularly interested in the situation stipulating the competences of the prosecutor when they learn about a crime that might have been committed. Tell me, is it correct that the absolute rule, a decision-maker about the situation and the course the investigation takes regarding a crime is the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: His decision could not be influenced by the Ministry of Interior, the police?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the prosecutor believes that the evidence is sufficient, then they file a motion to start an investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If they are completely clear that the evidence does not indicate that the crime has been committed, then the criminal report is rejected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: They may request from the police for additions of the criminal report with more evidence or to drop it, to reject it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that situation, when the evidence is insufficient, they could obtain new evidence on their own or through other bodies, but most frequently this is down through the bodies of the Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Most frequently, yes, but it depends on it's type of the criminal act, so we may ask also the customs administrations, various ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you are seeking verification of some facts or admission of additional information, or if you are seeking that additional actions are taken, the prosecutor's office always addresses the bodies from within the Ministry of Interior that are directly involved in detection of crimes and perpetrators of crime, so the departments of the Ministry of Interior or the sectors for Internal Affairs of a given city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Depending on the criminal charges or report who has filed the criminal report, that is the service that the police contacts with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The ministry, at a state level, generally does not have duties and responsibilities to take certain actions related to criminal offences and perpetrators. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. That are the police stations. It used to be like that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And especially the minister does not have any effective role to play in the detection of crime and perpetrators. He's, if you could agree with me, mainly a political figure who manages the ministry as a whole, while does not run effective control over the persons who are detecting crime and perpetrators thereof. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. For example, for more than ten years as a prosecutor, I have not conducted any minister in that time in respect to my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that the investigation is open only -- only against a particular person, and only upon reasonable ground to suspect that they have committed a crime that is prosecuting ex officio. So the perpetrator must be known?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you now to look at the Article 150 in 1D-1977, Macedonian, and 1D-1999. That is the Article 150, and that is the Article that stipulates what you have just stated, that the investigation is opened only against a perpetrator who is known. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The following Article, Article 151, says that the investigation is conducted only upon a proposal by the public prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of transcript, this Article is found on Macedonian page 1D-1978, and the English, 1D-1999 to 1D-2000. Page 20, line 3, I'm not sure that the translation is accurate, because my question is, and it is noted in the legal provision, that the investigation is run only against a known perpetrator, while in this line it is noted that the investigation is open only against a particular person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the investigating judge brings a decision to conduct an investigation, could you agree with me then the investigating judge is the dominus litis, the one who makes the decisions about all activities that need to be taken in the course of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: The investigating judge passes a decision to initiate a -- an investigation not a ruling, and the other part of the question is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge has the duty to tender all the evidence that the Prosecutor proposes, also the defence; and they could also decide on tendering their own evidence, is that correct, or taking their own actions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior does not have any competences and could make no requests to the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Especially, the Minister of the Interior has no competences over the investigating judge or the court?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, the situation is quite the opposite. The investigating judge could request the police to take certain actions, and then the police has the duty to render assistance to the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes..

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask now -- ask you now to look in the same binder under the same number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Article 170 -- INTERPRETER: Interpreter's correction: 180.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Macedonian page 1D -- 170 is what I said. And it is located in 1D-1983, and the English on the page 1D-2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have just answered my previous question. So tell me whether this is the provision of the Law on Criminal Procedure that establishes that the investigating judge may ask for assistance to be rendered from a body within the Ministry of Interior and that they have the duty to render that assistance?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, but not only from the police, but from any other state body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And briefly, with one or two more questions, we will dwell on the Law on Criminal Procedure. The investigating judge who has stated is running a procedure related to a person and an offence with regards to which the prosecutor asked that the procedure is open. But is it correct that if the investigating judge, in the course of the actual investigation, learns that some other criminal offence has been perpetrated or another perpetrator was involved, then they have the duty to inform the public prosecutor about that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They do not have any obligation and never do it in the practice to inform a body of the Ministry of Interior about that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. They inform the public prosecutor's office. When the investigating judge has enough evidence in that -- in his information, the public prosecutor can expand the investigation for one more criminal act or for one more person. The police has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police would have something to do with it only if the public prosecutor, as stipulated in 144 of Law on Criminal Procedure which prescribes describes the competences, would request the police to render any assistance?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: If the investigating judge learns something, he informs the public prosecutor on that. If the findings of the investigating judge are insufficient to expand the investigation against another person or for another act, then the public prosecutor could request the police to conduct certain examinations; that is to say, to gather evidence that will be needed by the public prosecutor. As I said, if they have enough evidence in the investigating procedure, then the public prosecutor does not inform the police, but files a request to -- to expand the investigation for another person or for another criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, otherwise, in the courtroom where the investigating judge presents the evidence, the public prosecutor is present as well, as the accused and the counsel for the accused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. And the public prosecutor is there only when there are serious criminal acts, actually the cases which include detention. Otherwise, we're not present at all of the investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But whether the public prosecutor is present or not, they make their own decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. The investigating judge sends an invitation and informs us about every investigation, when the investigation would start, and at what time. So we are informed, and it is up to us whether we are going to be present at the investigation or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigating judge never informs a minister of the Interior about any investigation or about any actions, and they could have no information about the statements that accused or a witness has made before the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No -- no, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the police also has no right to perform inspection of the court documents.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: They can just inspect the court files. Only the authorised counsel can do it, and the accused himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just said that the investigating judge could request some actions to be taken by the Ministry of Interior; and if they do not request this, then the Ministry of Interior has no legal possibility to learn what was important within that procedure or to take any actions that they are not authorised for. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that, as you stated, the investigation is conducted against a known perpetrator. Is it correct in situations when the perpetrator is unknown, the court can take only certain investigative measures upon a proposal of the public prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision to take investigating actions such as exhumation and post-mortem could be made only by the competent court and only upon a proposal of the public prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask that we see what you have just testified about in the Article 148; in the Macedonian, page 1D-1977, and the English page 1D-1999. That is the Article 148, which speaks about the only possibilities that the prosecutor and the judge have in a situation where the perpetrator is unknown. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was no legal possibility for the police to make a motion to the investigating judge suggesting that certain investigating actions are taken; and if that would happen, for the Prosecutor and for the judge, this could only be an initiative for them to start doing their own job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Would you -- would you please make the question more precise? What exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We said that the Prosecutor can request the carrying out of a certain investigative activity; is that correct? The Ministry of Interior, that is the police, cannot make such a request of the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Should the police, for example, submit a request to the public prosecutor to carry out an exhumation and the post-mortem, the prosecutor would understand this as an initiative, an attempt, by the police to encourage the prosecutor to carry out his legal duty; that is, to submit such a request to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. That will only be considered an initiative.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Ruskovska, please tell me, is it correct that an investigating judge can undertake certain investigative activities even before he issues a decision on the conduct of an investigation, most often questioning the accused or carrying out an on-site investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: So an on-site investigation is conducted when there are certain information that an act has been committed, a criminal act has been commit, severe criminal act with legal consequences most often. And the on-site inspection does not mean that a criminal charge will follow. It is possible that the perpetrator is dead, so the very on-site investigation of the prosecutor and the investigating judge does not necessarily mean a filing of a criminal charges. So if after the on-site investigation we have a perpetrator who can be accused, then the police files a criminal report against that person to the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back to what you have just explained, would it be correct to say that if the police were to learn of an event that might be a criminal offence, they would have to inform the public prosecutor and the investigating judge immediately, and it would be up to them then to decide whether to carry out an on-site investigation or not?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: So when an authorised official would learn about the commitment of a certain criminal ability, they inform the duty operative centre. The duty operative centre calls the public prosecutor on duty and informs him about the event, what has happened, and the place where it has happened; then it is up to the public prosecutor to decide whether an on-site investigation is needed, or the investigation will be left to the police. If the public prosecutor thinks it is necessary to make an on-site investigation, then they inform the investigating judge and then they do the on-site investigation jointly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So by informing the investigating judge and the prosecutor, the police have performed their legal duty, and the further decision is up to the prosecutor and the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the investigating judge decides to carry out an on-site investigation himself, he is the only organ setting up an investigation team, and he decides on everything done in the investigation. The police are only there to assist him. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: If the public prosecutor and the investigating judge go on the site, then depending on the nature of the crime, the investigating judge informs the post-mortem doctor on duty, the biologist, the chemist, the crime scene techniques, and everything that is needed in order to conduct the on-site investigation. So all the experts that are needed on the spot, with the very investigation, the very investigation is managed by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, in this situation, the police assist the court?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. It only assists, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask us to look at document -- the document under tab 5. This document is 65 ter 103, Macedonian page N000-7352, and English N000-73P2-ET [as interpreted]. May we look at the second page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know Dr. Zlatko Jackovski from the Institute for Forensic Medicine?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the first page, again, you will see that it says here that, "On the 12th of August, 2001, at about 1800 hours, we were informed by the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev, from primarily court Skopje I, that in the village of Ljuboten, region of Skopje, we should go out for an on-site inspection where five dead bodies of Albanian terrorists were located." If we look at this first sentence, in connection with what you have just said, is it correct that the investigating judge, in fact, when he decided to carry out this on-site investigation, invited the experts of the Institute of Forensic Medicine to accompany him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I already said, and I will repeat it. So always when it is -- if there is a doubt that a murder has been committed, there may be a suicide with a fire-arms, always the post-mortem doctors are called together with the investigating judge and with the deputy public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please look at the previous number in this binder, number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 153, N000-7344, and English is N000-7344-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Milan Gelevski?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. We worked together for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was also a deputy public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, both of us were deputies of the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This Official Note of the 15th of August, 2001, if you take a look at it, shows, does it not, that the deputy prosecutor also tried to go on-site with the investigating judge and carry out an on-site investigation in the village of Ljuboten; but for the reasons listed in this Official Note, the investigation was not carried out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please go back for yet another tab, number 3. This is 1D6.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Macedonian page number -- this is Exhibit 1D6, and the page is N000-7351; that's the second page of the document. In English, it's N000-7351-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know Ognen Stavrev, do you not? Ognen Stavrev, in 2001, was the investigating judge in Basic Court II in Skopje; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at where it says regarding the same case on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge says that he was informed by the Ministry of Interior, the sector in Skopje, the duty operations centre 92, that there are grounds to suspect that there are dead bodies in the village of Ljuboten, and he consulted the deputy public prosecutor, Roska Karova. Do you know this lady?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. We work together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And just like Dr. Zlatko Jackovski, the judge states here that on the 12th of August, it was not possible to carry out an on-site investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is what this report shows.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision on whether there are -- the required security conditions for an on-site investigation is made by the judge, is it not?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, in coordination with the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police cannot influence the decision of the court, can it?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's look at the first page of this same document, 1D6.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page N000-7350 in Macedonian, and in English it is probably already on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this Official Note. In the second paragraph, the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev; as we have just seen your colleague, Milan Gelevski, deputy prosecutor; and Dr. Zlatko Jackovski also attempted to carry out an on-site investigation in the village of Ljuboten; and if you can take a brief look, for the reason stated here, no investigation was carried out on-site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. The inspection was not carried out. At that time, we were on duty, when all these things were happening, and I think that you should ask Milan about it. As far as I can remember now - I don't know how precise this could be, because a lot of time has passed since then - Milan was telling us that someone was insisting to make an on-site investigation. Now, who was the one insisting, I don't know. Whether that was the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, whether the police was insisting, I really can't remember now. A lot of time has passed since then. But that -- together with the investigating judge and with the criminal pathologist, they have decided not to go there because of the danger. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just put one more question about this. Do you have any knowledge from that time? Did you learn from your colleagues when they set out towards the village for the third time that they learned that the bodies had been buried?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this might be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Your questioning has now gone for an hour and a quarter, so we expect that you will be fairly quick in finishing when we resume. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour..

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Ruskovska, in connection with the decision as to whether there are security conditions for an investigation, I would like to ask you the following. Do you know Dragoljub Sakic?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He's a colleague of yours from the prosecutors's office, is he not?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell Your Honours whether something happened to your colleague, and as a result of this, your prosecutor decided that prosecutors should not go to carry out on-site investigations in places where there's a security risk?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I know that they were supposed to go to an on-site inspection, and they were together with an investigating judge. I can't remember who was the investigating judge. Probably Sakic, if he is called here as a witness, will tell you himself. They went to an on-site investigation with three Hummers. So one was in the front; then Sakic, with the investigating judge, in the one in the middle; and behind them, there was another Hummer. And the first Hummer stepped on a land-mine placed on the road, and one of the police officers sustained a light injury. The convoy stopped. First, due to security reasons, they stayed inside the Hummers for about half an hour, because they did not know whether it was a siege by terrorists; and then after half an hour later, when they saw that there was no shooting, they went out of the Hummers, and then they walked for ten kilometres or more. I can't know how many kilometres exactly they were walking and making their way through the woods, until they managed to establish a contact with our security forces who escorted them back to Skopje. And I am not sure, but I think that that was the reason; and after this event the public prosecutor of Skopje at that time, Djoko Nastovski, decided that we would not go to on-site investigations any longer because we were not guaranteed. Nobody could guarantee or safety, and it was the same for the investigating judges. So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for explaining this. So there was one of the reasons why judges, under certain conditions, decided not to carry out on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I would only like to add, if I may, we did go to on-site investigations before that, regardless of the risk involved, before this. My colleagues would go to the border places that were more or less accessible. They would go there with helicopters, but they had bullet-proof vests and helmets on their heads. And until that event, until this took place with Sakic, we would go, really; but after this, it was obvious that our safety could not be guaranteed. So after that event, we stopped going to on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the event you have described occurred a few days before -- before Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I couldn't say precisely, really. Sakic said and remembers the exact date, so you will need to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We also spoke about criminal proceedings in which you, as deputy prosecutor, participated. Is it correct that before questioning an accused, the investigating judge informs him of all his legal rights, and all of you who participated in criminal proceedings did your best to have all these rights respected fully?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: If it weren't like this, this would be a violation of the criminal procedure, so the records of it would not be valid evidence for the court. This would be in breach of the criminal proper, and the very fact of a breach of criminal procedure considers the evidence being invalid before the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the Prosecutor, P235, you said that you were on duty when the inspector from the SVR Skopje, Mr. Bojic, informed you of the fact that criminal reports against a certain number of persons would be submitted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just clarify. I was not on duty. These were my regular working hours; and since this was the time of summer holidays, we were only seven of us working within that period. So all of us were working then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your statement correctly, you succeeded in convincing Mr. Bojic that not just one but several criminal reports should be submitted, because one deputy public prosecutor would not be able to deal with the number of people reported; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I'm correct, the police accepted this suggestion, and three criminal reports were filed against 27 persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you yourself wrote one of those requests to institute an investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the microphone is moved closer to the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show, or rather, look at the document under tab 6 in your binder. That's P46. The Macedonian version is on page 0463-8774-035. The English version is on page ET 0463-8808, page 1, please. This is in Macedonian, and P46 is the page in English, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wish to ask you, in connection with this document, is this the criminal report submitted in this form by the competent organ of the Interior to you, as the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top of the page, we have information about the organ submitting the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And one can see from this that the criminal charges were brought by the Department of the Interior in Cair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that such a criminal report is accompanied by the evidence available to the police?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of this, you decide whether to submit a request for a criminal investigation to be started, or you decide to act in other ways; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that the Ministry of Interior of the competent organ of the ministry, should they come up with additional information concerning the criminal report, subsequently deliver to you the additional information and evidence that was not sent along with the criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: For instance, if these are cases involving detention, and I'm speaking about detention with longer duration, that is customary. The police could not manage everything. They must prepare the report within 24 hours and then submit it to the competent public prosecutor. So, normally, the expert reports are delayed, and then afterwards they submit to us an additional report; that is, the supplement to the criminal report. And through this they inform us about the additional evidence that they acquired.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look at number 8 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's P46, number 0463-8874-044, and the English is ET 0463-8817-0463-8817.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is additional material sent by the police to the prosecutor in connection with a previously submitted criminal report. Is this an example of what you have just talked about; an expert report was submitted, or something along those lines, and the police then subsequently then sent this to you?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we have just said that in the courtroom, there is the chamber and the prosecutor and the defence counsel. But is it also true that order in the court, the bringing of the accused, and so on is seen to by the court police?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the binder under number 44, could you please look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a 65 ter document, 376. In Macedonian, the first page is N002-5405. In English, the first page is N002-5406-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please look at Roman 8, Judicial Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Macedonian, it is N002-5424; and in English, N002-5426-ET?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which page did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 6. 44, towards the end. This is the Law on Courts.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 103. The heading above that is "Court Police."

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My first question is: The status of the court police is regulated by the Law on Courts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The court police, in 2001, and probably still today, falls within the competence of the Ministry of Justice. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior has no competences with regard to the court police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Ruskovska, persons who are being detained are in the court detention unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. Detention -- the detention is in the remand prison, not in the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am not referring to the court building, but to the remand prison.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And detention and remand falls within the competence of the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: All courts or all prison institutions including the remand prison, as well as the employees or the guards and all the employees, are employees of the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just have answered what my next question was going to be. The guards in prison fall within the competence of the Ministry of Justice; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior, the police, has no competences, either with respect to remand prisons or to guards in prisons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Not only that they don't have any competence; but, for example, if they would like to interview a detainee or a sentenced person in the prison, they have to ask for permission from the judged or the presiding judge if the case is ongoing. So they can't each enter the prison without permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: They certainly have no powers over prison guards?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No, they don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You may recall, in 2001, the Minister of Justice was an Albanian, Ixet Memeti.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that, at that time, there were several ministers who were Albanian and several deputy ministers who were Albanian?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not hear or probably you do not know that any minister or deputy minister who was an Albanian resigned at the time?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As you said, that you submitted a request for the undertaking of an investigation with respect to some persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the documents under tab 12 in the binder. That's P52. Macedonian page 4. English page N001- -- ET N001-9900-N001-9901. And please look at N001-9897-05, and English ET-N001-9900-2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is this your name? Were you the signatory of this request to open an investigation?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the usual kind of request submitted by a deputy prosecutor to an investigating judge to have an investigation conducted with respect to certain persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you have just said, when explaining detention on remand, you said that this is also done at the request of the prosecutor. So this kind of request is also included in this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior and the minister himself have no authority to propose or decide on detention or remand for certain persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were present when statements were taken from a number of suspects. These were the suspects for whom you submitted a request for an investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now show you only the first pages of some statements made by suspects. I don't want us to get into a discussion of what you did concerning these individual statements. I will just put some general questions to you after we have seen the documents. So please look first under tab 13 in your binder, Exhibit P54.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Macedonian page N001-9643-045, and English N001-9687-ET-001. And then under tab 14, you see Exhibit P52. In Macedonian, it's page 11. In English, it's ET-001-9907-1. And then please look at tab 15. That's Exhibit P52. I apologise. There's a mistake here -- oh, no. It's all right. It's all right. It's been corrected. So in tab 15, we have P52. Macedonian page 14, and English page ET-001-9910-1. And then in tab 16, that's Exhibit P52. Macedonian page 30; English page N001-9916-1. And then tab 17, Exhibit P52. Macedonian page 17, English page ET-001-9913-1. And then under tab 18, Exhibit P52. Macedonian page 23, English page ET-N001-9919-1. Tab 19, Exhibit P52. Macedonian page 26, English page ET-N001-9922-1. Tab 20, Exhibit P52. Macedonian page 29, English page ET-N001-9925-1. And in tab 21, Exhibit P53. Macedonian page 16, English page N001-9842-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I tried to read slowly to give you time to look at these first pages. Tell me, Ms. Ruskovska, did you notice that on those front pages it says that you were present when these persons were questioned as deputy public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So all of these suspects were questioned in your presence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge informed them about all their legal rights, and that was done in your presence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were warned that they had the right to speak in Albanian language and that they had the right to an attorney, but everybody stated that they spoke Macedonian and that they would defend themselves in Macedonian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were also informed that they had a right to counsel of their own choice; and since most of them could not afford one, the court then assigned them an ex officio counsel who was present in the questioning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were also informed that they can refrain from answering the questions, and that they could present their own defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge, and it was done in your presence, recorded in the minutes from the trial everything that the suspects stated with regards to the investigation that was conducted against them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the court record accurately shows everything that these persons stated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Ruskovska, that pursuant to our law, an accused could never be questioned as a witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. I mean, it is correct, they could not be interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They are never informed that they have the duty to speak the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As opposed to the witnesses, and if the witnesses perjure themselves before the court, they could be held responsible for perjury, the accused pursuant to the law of the Republic of Macedonia could never be held for a false testimony given to the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in all these cases, the court record is dictated by the judge out loud and the accused are asked if they have something to add to it?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Not only in these records, but all the records that are made by the investigating judge are dictated out loud; and then the accused, or a witness, or anyone giving a statement has the right to read it before signing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if by chance the investigating judge would omit something from the record, then the prosecutor who is present has the right and also the defence counsel have the right as well as the accused himself or herself they have the right to ask that the issue omitted is recorded in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if anyone stated in your presence that they have been, for instance, ill-treated, then the judge included that in the records; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if those -- if such facts are not indicated in the records, you can say with certainty that the accused never mentioned any ill-treatment?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When making a statement to the Prosecutor on the 16th of December, 2002 [as interpreted], you were shown the statement of the accused, Ali Riza, where he indicated that he had been ill-treated and beaten while the paraffin glove was performed on him. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: I remember it was December, but I can't remember who was exactly saying that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Maybe I made a mistake. In line 22, it is written "2002," while it should be "2005," when you made your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In that statement, in item 11, P235, you stated that the customary practice for anyone accused from that area is that they say before the court that they admitted to something or they stated something because they had been ill-treated or because the police beat them. Tell me, is that practically the customary practice, the foundation on which the accused are trying to base their defence?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: It is like that even today. We have, for example, a statement at a main hearing when the accused would say that the investigating judge has beaten them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the evidence available to the court and to the prosecutor clearly indicate that it is not correct, considering the right of the accused to present any evidence that they deem appropriate, no measures could be taken against the accused for perjuring themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your statement, you note that if the accused, one who would claim ill-treatment, had no visible injuries, then you and the investigating judge would simply consider that they were lying?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption, but it seems right now that my learned friend is simply asking the witness to confirm what she has -- the contents of her written statement which are already in evidence, and I'm not sure whether this is the best use of our court time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have anticipated me by about three minutes, Mr. Saxon. I will 5.00 in my sights as a convenient time to interrupt and point out that much of what you're now saying is already in evidence, and it's not going to help anybody to just put it into evidence again. The statement is there so that could I ask you, Ms. Residovic, to now concentrate on any remaining matters that have not been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will act now with -- in accordance with the instructions of Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The main thing I wish to ask you, Ms. Ruskovska, considering the facts that you have already stated in the statement given to the Prosecutor, is whether the facts that were stated by the accused, in your presence and in the presence of the investigating judge and of the counsel, were available to the Ministry of Interior or to the police?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: You mean about the statements given before the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: No. I mean, they were not available to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that is only normal, because the police did not participate in an investigation. Also the post-mortem report were never sent to the police, they were sent to the investigating judge only. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMA RUSKOVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
